evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.field: 形義通解；《說文》字形與早期用例
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 星 as 从晶、生聲 and reports the original sense as “star.” It cites oracle-bone inscription 合集15625反, 庚辰星(晴), as a weather-clear use; cites the *Shijing* 鄘風 “星言夙駕” with 星 used for clear weather; and records a Western Zhou bronze-inscription use as a personal name in 麓伯簋. This supports distinct star and clear-weather uses, but does not by itself date the first occurrence of either meaning.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：星

evidence.source: 臺灣中央研究院漢字構形資料庫
evidence.text: The record lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu bamboo/silk, seal, and Shuowen variant forms for 星, but its text view does not expose the glyph images or an explanation of individual transitions. No glyph image was visually inspected for this research.
evidence.title: 漢字「星」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫；《說文解字》 entry reproduced by Taiwan Ministry of Education variant dictionary
evidence.text: The sources give the traditional account 曐/星 “from 晶, 生 as phonetic,” with 晶 conveying the star array and 生 serving as sound; the same Shuowen entry also offers an alternative pictographic explanation. The dossier’s claim that 日 itself is the semantic component is therefore an oversimplification of the cited traditional analysis. The modern lower 日 shape is not enough to establish an original 日 component.
evidence.kind: historical lexicographic account, attributed to Shuowen
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》：星

evidence.source: 漢語國學, Shuowen text with attached 《說文新證》 note
evidence.text: The attached modern note says oracle-bone 星 was first written 晶, depicting a cluster of shining stars, then 生 was added as a phonetic and the graphs differentiated; it describes variable counts of star-shaped elements, a fixed three-star pattern in bronze and seal forms, and reduction to one star in Warring States forms. This specific sequence is an attributed scholarly interpretation, not an independently inspected glyph analysis here. It conflicts in emphasis with catalog summaries that describe oracle-bone examples as star elements plus 生 from the outset.
evidence.kind: secondary paleographic analysis reproduced in a dictionary entry
evidence.title: 星的说文解字解释

evidence.source: 漢字「星」字形演變字源（compiled paleographic references）
evidence.text: This page describes two oracle-bone forms as star depictions plus phonetic 生, later bronze/Warring States forms as predecessors of seal forms, and certain Warring States forms as simplified from 晶 with 生 phonetic. It also says 晶 was later reduced to 日 and classifies the graph as phonosemantic. Its exact account differs from the 《說文新證》 note’s sequence in which an earlier 晶-only graph acquired 生; the available text does not resolve whether these statements concern different early variants or competing reconstructions.
evidence.title: 星字形演变字源

evidence.text: The page’s transcribed Shuowen volume 7 text is the historical lexicographic source for the account: “萬物之精，上爲列星。从晶，生聲,” alongside an alternative pictographic analysis. This is evidence for what the Han dictionary asserts, not automatic proof of the character’s original formation.
evidence.kind: primary historical dictionary text in modern transcription
evidence.title: 說文解字/07

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction, appendix table
evidence.field: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese entry for 星
evidence.text: The supplied local Baxter–Sagart table row for 星 is xīng, MC seng, OC *s-tsʰˤeŋ, gloss ‘star’ (GSR 0812x). The externally inspected Baxter–Sagart table independently displays the same 星 reading and reconstruction. Do not merge this with Zhengzhang *sleːŋ or with other systems’ readings.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction, appendix table
evidence.field: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese entry for 生
evidence.text: The local Baxter–Sagart table provided in the input has no 生 row, so no local 生 reconstruction is asserted. The externally inspected Baxter–Sagart table gives 生 MC sraeng and OC *sreŋ (with a note on possible *s.reŋ analysis), distinct from 星 *s-tsʰˤeŋ. These same-system forms have a similar final but differ in onset structure; the graph’s phonetic role is supported by the character dictionaries, while exact historical sound development should not be collapsed into modern Mandarin resemblance.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.source: Unihan local row supplied in research input; Unicode Unihan documentation
evidence.text: The supplied local row is 星 kMandarin xīng (sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt; row for U+661F, field kMandarin). Unicode documents kMandarin as a Unihan reading property, but the required official per-character GetUnihanData page could not be accessed in this browser session. The click-through URL is supplied for later verification; the local row is not represented as an externally inspected Unicode character record.
evidence.kind: local structured reading with external lookup limitation
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup: U+661F (attempted; inaccessible)

evidence.source: Unihan local row supplied in research input; Unicode Unihan documentation
evidence.text: No local kMandarin row for 生 was supplied in the input, and the repository fallback extract is not present in the research packet. No exact local modern reading row for 生 is therefore claimed. Unicode describes kMandarin as a current Mandarin-reading property; the official per-character lookup for U+751F was inaccessible in this session.

evidence.text: Unicode’s documentation identifies Unihan_Readings.txt as the source file for reading properties including kMandarin. This verifies the nature and provenance of the field, but not the value for a particular character.
evidence.title: UAX #38: Unicode Han Database (Unihan)

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction
evidence.field: § discussion of 星 and proposed sound/semantic relation to 晴 and 清
evidence.text: The authors reconstruct 星 ‘star’ as *s-tsʰˤeŋ and propose a prefixed deverbal analysis related to a root *tsʰˤeŋ ‘bright’; they discuss 星 as a loan graph for 晴 *N-tsʰeŋ and compare 清 *tsʰˤeŋ ‘clear’. This is a proposed linguistic analysis, not settled semantic chronology. A 2019 critique notes the large semantic gap between ‘clear’ adjectives and ‘star’, and says that the needed intermediate ‘clear sky/night sky’ sense is only a possible reading of a Shijing passage. Therefore do not present the derivation as established.
evidence.kind: primary scholarly phonological analysis, with disputed semantic proposal
evidence.title: Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction (accessible excerpt)

evidence.source: Bulletin of Chinese Linguistics 12 (2019), article excerpt
evidence.field: critique of proposed 星–晴–清 relationship
evidence.text: The article questions the semantics of deriving ‘star’ from a ‘clear’ root: it says 晴 and 清 do not mean ‘bright’ or associate with stars, and treats a ‘clearing in the night sky’ intermediate as a possible but unproven explanation. This is a material caveat on the Baxter–Sagart proposal; the character’s phonetic analysis and the proposed lexical etymology are separate questions.
evidence.title: Bulletin of Chinese Linguistics 12 (2019), pp. 13–28

evidence.source: 韻典網, Zhengzhang Shangfang system; comparative entry surfaced in inspected character page
evidence.text: The Zhengzhang reconstruction shown for 星 is *sleːŋ. It is a separate reconstruction system from Baxter–Sagart *s-tsʰˤeŋ; the distinct notations must not be silently combined or corrected into one another. The site identifies its data as Zhengzhang’s *Shanggu Yinxi* and notes editorial normalization in its digital presentation.
evidence.title: 上古音系 — 韻典網

evidence.source: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》
evidence.text: The entry quotes 鄘風《定之方中》 “星言夙駕” and glosses the phrase as travelling by starlight at night. Other cited interpretation in the HKBU dictionary database takes 星 here as ‘clear weather.’ The phrase is therefore an ambiguous early semantic witness; it should not alone prove either a distinct ‘clear’ sense or ‘starry sky’ sense.
evidence.kind: historical lexicographic interpretation of a classic passage
evidence.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》：星言夙駕

evidence.source: 漢典, 《康熙字典》 and Shuowen annotations
evidence.field: entry citations and later semantic extensions
evidence.text: The entry documents classical astronomical senses and later developments including scattered points, star-like small or bright objects, rapid movement by comparison with a shooting star, night/night travel, and a clear-weather interpretation of the Shijing phrase. These are cited historical uses, not a chronology inferable from the page’s gloss order. The 《說文》 quotation repeats both phonosemantic and alternative pictographic accounts.
evidence.title: 星 xīng — 漢典

gaps: The web research used 18 distinct search queries, the stated maximum. Searches after the initial 12 targeted remaining material questions: reconstruction disagreement, semantic derivation critique, and exact Unihan lookup.

Exact oracle-bone glyphs were not visually inspected. Paleographic statements about the count and arrangement of star elements are reported as source claims, and the disagreement over when 生 entered the graph remains unresolved.

The cited oracle-bone number and Shijing passage are available, but the opened sources do not provide a securely dated first occurrence for each sense. No chronology is inferred from dictionary sense order.

Whether early 晶 and 星 were one graph with variant forms, or a pictograph and a differentiated phonetic spelling, remains disputed in the inspected accounts. No evidence of graphic corruption was found; reduction from 晶-like star clusters to 日 is described as simplification, not demonstrated corruption.
The Shijing 星言夙駕 is semantically disputed between ‘by starlight/at night’ and ‘when the weather cleared’; it cannot establish a single unambiguous semantic link.

Baxter–Sagart’s proposed lexical derivation of star from a clear/bright root is disputed and its semantic bridge is not established. This uncertainty does not negate the independently attested 生 phonetic role in dictionary analyses.

Official Unicode GetUnihanData pages for U+661F and U+751F could not be accessed; the exact local 星 kMandarin row was supplied, while a local 生 row was not. Unicode per-character click-through values remain unverified.
No inspected source established an independent pronunciation/name for the original star depiction; no whole-graph phonetic-loan claim requiring recovery of a depicted object’s name is made here.
No bulk-reuse terms for the paleographic/dictionary sites were verified. No local extract is recommended; character-specific citations and concise paraphrases suffice.
